question.problem:
Given the matrix 
$V=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(V).$
question.worked_solution:
In order to find a basis of $\text{Col}(V),$ we reduce the matrix $V$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $2$nd columns are pivot columns, while the $3$rd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one. 

The $1$st and $2$nd columns from the original matrix are ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}.$ So, a basis of $\text{Col}(V)$ is $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\},$ that is to say, 

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}.
$$
